paper: Can Large Language Models Mine Interpretable Financial Factors More Effectively? A Neural-Symbolic Factor Mining Agent Model
headline_mechanism: FAMA combines correlation-diverse cross-sample selection with a RankIC-ordered chain of experience to guide symbolic factor generation; FAMA(CI-7) is the strongest headline configuration in Table 1.

source_anchors.claim: Factors are evaluated by cross-sectional rank correlation between formation exposure and subsequent return.
CSS clusters factors by correlation-related distance and draws diverse context factors from different categories.
Experience chains order factors by RankIC and retain a newly generated factor when it improves on the matched chain.
The experiment starts from Alpha101-style factors, uses seven categories and two cross-samples, and highlights the seven-iteration combined CSS/CoE configuration.

preserved_elements: symbolic price/volume factor seeds and a fixed arithmetic expression grammar
approximated_elements: six available JKP price/volume characteristics replace 38 unreleased paper-selected Alpha101 seeds
correlation of trailing monthly candidate RankIC paths replaces correlation of the paper's factor-value vectors
a deterministic four-operator grammar replaces text-davinci-002 symbolic generation
a 60-month rolling history replaces the paper's fixed 2015-2019 training interval
the top two diverse experience representatives are rank-combined into one stock score
invented_elements: the exact six JKP seed identities
the identity, pairwise mean, difference, and product candidate grammar
deterministic farthest-first seven-medoid grouping of RankIC histories
minimum 24 finite training RankIC months and numerical tie-breaking
common monthly value-weighted long/short decile portfolio and costs
portfolio_adapter: Frozen us_jkp_headline_v1 top-1000 monthly value-weighted long/short deciles with 10 bp one-way primary cost.
claim_boundary: This is a researcher-authored FAMA-inspired symbolic-search reconstruction, not the unreleased FAMA model, its generated factors, or a reproduction of the paper's reported return and RankIC results.
